population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic, 2032 cohort (27.9 on, 9.1 off): 60% of the 27.9 stay on (16.7) and 11.2 stop, giving a pool of 11.2 + 9.1 = 20.3. Of that pool 57% restart (11.6) and 8.7 stay off, so the old cohort has 16.7 + 11.6 = 28.3 on. New ever-users number 4.8 pts: 3.8 on and 1.0 already off. On = 28.3 + 3.8 = 32.1. Off = 8.7 + 1.0 = 9.7. Ever = 37.0 + 4.8 = 41.8, and 41.8 − 32.1 = 9.7. Cycled = 13.4 pts (2032) + ~5.0 first-time restarters in the old cohort + ~0.4 among new starters = 18.8 of 41.8 ever-users = 45%. Persistence held at 60% because public coverage replaced cash for many. The restart rate held at 57% because the Medicaid metabolic option and permanent Medicare coverage reopened doors. Verified-dose lockouts closed others. Of ~270M adults, ~86.7M are on drug, ~26.2M have used and are off (a growing share locked out by verified-dose rules rather than stopping by choice) and ~157M have never used. The never-users include a self-described 'natty' constituency, people with contraindications, uninsured adults in the ten states without the Medicaid metabolic option, and people who refused DEXA-gated Medicare continuation. Age bands weighted by adult shares (20/33/24/23%): 3.80 + 11.48 + 11.76 + 5.06 = 32.1. 65+ rose 17 → 22 (~13.7M) as permanent Medicare coverage and the dementia label outweighed the bone wave. Income thirds: (37 + 32.5 + 26.8)/3 = 32.1. The bottom third rose most (+5.1) through Medicaid. Pediatric: 1.5% of ~73M ≈ 1.1M, ~210k of them aged 6–11, most of them Medicaid-covered. The first children born to parents who were both on drug at conception (with coded planned interruptions) are now in kindergarten.

access.public_coverage: The Medicare Metabolic Health Act (Nov 2033) replaced the Bridge with permanent Part D obesity coverage from Jan 2034. The blended plan payment is $195/month across semaglutide, tirzepatide, retatrutide and oral products, including dispensing, with a $35 copay. Continuation requires ≥5% loss at month 6, ≥80% verified-dose adherence (connected pen log, or PDC as fallback) and annual DEXA for 65+. Medicare pays 17% of fills ≈ 14.7M users (≈13.3M aged 65+ plus ~1.4M disabled under-65). Gross: 14.7M × $195 × 12 ≈ $34.4B/yr. Copays: 14.7M × $35 × 12 ≈ $6.2B. Net program ≈ $28.2B. The Act also created an optional Medicaid 'metabolic health option' at 80% FMAP, adopted by 40 states plus DC. Twelve of those states attach verified-dose adherence waivers. Medicaid pays 15% ≈ 13.0M users at $185 blended: 13.0M × $185 × 12 ≈ $28.9B combined, federal share ~78% ≈ $22.5B. The HRSA Community Incretin Access Program got $4.2B for FY2034 (down from $5.0B), and the rider now requires a quarterly in-person visit, though still no weight-progress test. It serves ≈3.5M: 2.3M generic liraglutide × $65 × 12 ≈ $1.79B, plus 1.2M semaglutide for cessation/AUD/gambling × $129 federal ceiling × 12 ≈ $1.86B, ≈ $3.65B. TRICARE/VA/DoD cover ≈2.6M, including ~165k active-duty members in the readiness programme: 165k × $129 × 12 ≈ $255M/yr.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 90+ semaglutide brands at $6–35/month, and generic tirzepatide is sold in India, Brazil, Turkey, Mexico and Egypt. Generic semaglutide is standard across Canada, Latin America and most of Asia. A Chinese originator triple agonist (NMPA 2033, ~29% loss at 80 weeks) is exported to Southeast Asia and the Gulf and has filed with the EMA. The WTO panel on India's mail-export complaint was established in 2033.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ~86.7M users: commercial 35% (30.3M), Medicare 17% (14.7M), Medicaid 15% (13.0M), HRSA 4% (3.5M), TRICARE/VA/DoD 3% (2.6M), cash/direct 16% (13.9M), gray 10% (8.7M) = 100%. Public payers (39%) now pay more fills than employers (35%), the first time this has happened, and Medicare is the largest single payer by spend. Managed decline continued: the Nov 2033 Strategic Supply Agreement renewal, which Lilly signed under scandal pressure and Novo matched, stepped TrumpRx/direct prices to $199 (semaglutide injection), $249 (tirzepatide), $299 (retatrutide) and $129 (oral starting doses), with $199 for oral maintenance. Wegovy list stays $1,349 and retatrutide list $1,499, and almost nobody pays list. Why there is still no US generic: the 2033 settlement entry dates depended on final ANDA approval. FDA issued complete-response letters to three synthetic-semaglutide filers in 2033 over peptide-impurity immunogenicity data, and only tentative approvals exist. First entry is now expected in 2035. Conditioning is moving from fills to injections. Both manufacturers now ship connected autoinjectors that log dose events. The Jan 2034 CMS rule accepts these 'verified-dose' logs for Medicare continuation and Medicaid waivers, and PBMs resell them to employers. About 68% of covering employers attach conditions. The Ninth Circuit struck PDC-based premium differentials in 2034 while the Fifth upheld them, and the resulting split now pushes employers toward verified-dose data. Skip-but-fill falls where pens are connected and persists on older pens, oral products and the gray market. Gray users dipped from ~9.0M to ~8.7M as retatrutide reached $299. 503A compounders ($89–179) remain the cheapest product for people locked out of public plans.

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The triple-agonist driver was realised through an existing product. Retatrutide (30.4% at 104 weeks on 12 mg) became the most common new start for BMI ≥35 once the SSA renewal priced it at $299 and Part D covered it from Jan 2034. Lilly paired it with its connected 'Link' pen. A Chinese originator triple agonist (~29%) launched in China and export markets and filed with the EMA, but has no US filing. Amycretin was approved Aug 2033 (~22% at 68 weeks) after Novo's remediation. Bimagrumab + tirzepatide (BLA Mar 2032) was approved Oct 2034 for adults ≥60 with obesity at high sarcopenia risk. Launch is Q1 2035 with Medicare pricing unresolved, so it is not yet on market. Amycretin oral and next-generation monthly triple agonists remain in phase 2/3 and are not on the US market. Semaglutide's gambling-disorder approval rested on two 26-week RCTs (reduced gambling days and spend, small effect sizes). In the March 2033 Lilly scandal, discovery in MDL 3094 showed that a TRIUMPH-4 extension scintigraphy substudy had found delayed gastric emptying persisting up to 12 weeks after stopping 12 mg retatrutide in a minority of participants. Lilly classified it as exploratory and kept it out of the sBLA summary.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Higher on retatrutide 12 mg, which is now the most common new start for BMI ≥35, and among gray users who skip titration.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction (mass tort)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Mass-tort scale. MDL 3094 has ~148,000 filed and tolled claims, up from ~61,000. The surge followed the March 2033 unsealing of Lilly's retatrutide 12 mg post-discontinuation scintigraphy substudy. Persistence beyond 12 weeks after stopping is still disputed at population level.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Dec 2033: FDA adds 'delayed gastric emptying may persist for weeks after discontinuation' to the retatrutide label, plus class language for doses above maintenance. Sep 2034: Novo announces a $4.1B no-admission settlement programme for semaglutide gastroparesis/ileus claims. Lilly has not settled. DOJ civil investigative demand to Lilly is pending. A Senate HELP hearing was held.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Absolute cases rise with retatrutide 12 mg uptake and faster loss.
Registries still show low absolute risk with no causal confirmation. The MDL pancreatitis track reached ~26,000 claims, carried by the gastroparesis surge.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; consolidated in MDL 3094. Excluded from Novo's settlement programme.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A new MDL track opened in 2034 with ~4,000 claims. Nordic, VA and Medicare-linked registries show no excess incidence through ten years.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No label change. FDA says the signal is not supported by current data.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A population problem, now larger in absolute terms as 65+ use reaches ~13.7M. Worst on liraglutide, compounded product and retatrutide without training or protein.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings retained. Medicare continuation requires a resistance-training referral. HRSA quarterly visits now include a grip-strength check. Bimagrumab + tirzepatide approved Oct 2034 (launch 2035).

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Medicare hip-fracture admissions rose another ~2% in 2032–33 and were flat in 2034 as antiresorptive cover spread. More 65+ users offset lower per-user risk. The final adolescent bone-accrual study (2033) confirmed lumbar-spine z-score accrual ~0.15–0.2 SD lower after more than 3 years. The share explained by weight loss itself is still disputed.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: DEXA Warnings retained. Pediatric labelling update (Oct 2033) adds bone-accrual monitoring for users under 18 on drug more than 2 years. Medicare pays for incretin and antiresorptive together, with no 75+ combination fracture-outcome trial.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; very low absolute risk.
No causal association, including in the BED, AUD and gambling-disorder trial populations.

A 2033 FDA pooled analysis of randomised data put the excess clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~0.8% at standard maintenance doses and ~4% at retatrutide ≥8 mg. Survey reports of 'reduced pleasure' fell to ~6–8% of long-term users after the 2033 obesity-medicine step-down guidance moved users to the lowest effective maintenance dose. Deliberate dose holidays fell from ~45% to ~28% as verified-dose pens made them visible.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Apr 2034 class labelling lists anhedonia as 'uncommon' at maintenance doses and 'common' at retatrutide ≥8 mg. SHAPS screening is recommended at the 6-month visit.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Increasingly driven by verified-dose lockouts and month-6 non-response cut-offs in Medicare and the twelve Medicaid adherence-waiver states.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Indiana waiver litigation unresolved. The Medicare Act allows one reinstatement after 6 months. No federal rule on Medicaid lockouts.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Protein, iron, B12 and vitamin D insufficiency signals persist and are higher on retatrutide 12 mg.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Medicare continuation counselling includes a protein target. HRSA visits add a dietary screen.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon, adolescent, pediatric and cycling effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of adult and eleven of adolescent follow-up. ~210k children aged 6–11 are on drug, and pubertal-timing data are still absent. Cyclers now make up 45% of ever-users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric registry ongoing. Bone monitoring labelled for under-18s.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Poison-centre calls are slightly down. Locked-out public-plan users switching to 503A compounded semaglutide keep dosing errors steady.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CBP seizures continue under Section 232. A second peptide-distributor indictment came in 2034. No user prosecutions.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg.
Off-label 'brain health' use among 50–64-year-olds without diabetes or CVD keeps growing, which helps explain 50–64 use reaching 49%.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label states the population limits. Medicare continuation rules do not distinguish on-label from off-label 'brain health' starts in 65+.

food_and_beverage.state: US packaged-food volume falls another ~2.5% a year. Snack divestitures to private equity are largely done, and PE owners now cut SKUs and shrink packs. Protein and 'bone-and-muscle' formats keep growing. A small 'natty' premium niche appears: regional bakeries, whole-milk dairies and 'full plate' frozen meals branded as unmedicated, strongest in Grand Rapids, Tulsa and Nashville. It is visible on shelves and negligible in national volume.

alcohol.state: The fifth and sixth consecutive years of US volume decline. ASAM's 2034 first-line AUD guidance and HRSA semaglutide for AUD reach the heaviest-drinking decile, which carries a disproportionate share of spirits volume. Distillers push exports, 'zero-proof' lines and tasting-room tourism. State excise forecasts cut again.

restaurants.state: Value chains keep closing suburban units. Fast casual's 'half plate' is standard. Natty 'full table' independents and church suppers grow locally with no national effect. Casino-resort food-and-beverage revenue softens as gambling-disorder treatment and lower appetite overlap.

apparel.state: Size runs keep widening. Uniform makers keep re-cutting. Fall-safe senior apparel is mainstream. A natty aesthetic of loose linen, high-waisted 'fed' denim and an open-circle pin is a profitable micro-niche for Tulsa and Brooklyn labels.

fitness.state: Resistance training is a covered condition of Medicare continuation and many employer plans. Low-cost gyms, PT chains and Medicare Advantage strength programmes grow. Gyms now sell 'referral compliance' attendance logs to plans, which mirrors the pen data.

insurance.state: Employer pharmacy trend falls to ~+6% as Medicare absorbs older and disabled users and the SSA prices fall. Plans move conditioning to verified-dose data after the Ninth Circuit ruling. PBMs sell 'dose-verification' feeds. Medicare Part D premiums rise ~$4/month on the new benefit.

pharma.state: Lilly remains the national champion but is under a DOJ demand, a Senate hearing and ~100k retatrutide-linked claims. Its 2033 SSA renewal concessions were widely read as the price of keeping the tariff exemption. Novo's $4.1B settlement and tariff burden squeeze margins, though amycretin gives it a new product. Generic semaglutide filers await final FDA approval. Connected-pen device revenue is a new line.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: The body now carries a log as well as a payer. A lean, muscled body with a clean verified-dose record and a DEXA history reads as compliant. A heavier body reads as locked out, priced out, or 'natty'. Natty has moved from bodybuilding slang to a general identity meaning never on an incretin, and it is claimed with pride.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Retatrutide at $299 and Part D coverage brought surgical-grade loss to the bottom two thirds, so 'pen-thin' without muscle now reads as Medicaid or Medicare-without-a-trainer. Among the affluent the marker has moved to the visible absence of effort: maintenance on the lowest dose, a private trainer, a natural-looking softness. Among women 65+ in Sun City, Arizona, the marker is still posture and a fall-free year.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: The natty movement has turned the Open Table suppers of Grand Rapids, Nashville and Tulsa into a weekly ritual with an aesthetic: long tables, bread broken by hand, no phones photographing plates, and an open-circle pin. Oakland and Brooklyn unmedicated supper clubs share the tables but not the theology. In medicated households 'family dinner' often means one adult eating and others keeping company.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles carry 'natty' or a molecule. Some apps add a filter. Couples on Medicare or conditioned employer plans now ask prescribers for coded 'planned interruptions' (up to 14 days a year in Medicare) around conception and anniversaries, because uncoded pauses show up in the pen log.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is clinical, contractual and now logged. For the natty movement it is a birthright ('fed and free'). For the gambling and AUD indications, craving has been redefined as one treatable dimension spanning food, drink, bets and carts. Seven states now have 'appetite liberty' laws barring employer premium conditioning. Five of them passed in 2033, among them Oklahoma, whose own Medicaid waiver still conditions coverage on verified doses.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. The 2033 FDA pooled analysis found excess clinically meaningful anhedonia of ~0.8% at maintenance doses and ~4% at retatrutide ≥8 mg. Survey 'reduced pleasure' fell from 10–15% to ~6–8% of long-term users after step-down maintenance guidance. Deliberate holidays fell from ~45% to ~28% as verified-dose pens made pauses visible. Telehealth 'quiet' subscriptions fell to ~0.8M. The Apr 2034 class label calls anhedonia 'uncommon' at maintenance doses. Clinics screen with SHAPS at month 6 and step patients down when they score positive.
interior_life.framing: A side effect: uncommon, dose-related, screened for and managed by stepping down. 'The grey' now sounds like 2031 slang. Pharmacists ask 'any flatness?' the way they ask about nausea. The gambling and AUD indications are framed as targeted 'craving reduction', and clinicians are careful to separate this from global flattening. The natty movement still says 'chemical contentment', but it now argues mainly about autonomy and surveillance rather than mood.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Sales staff no longer time holidays to quarter-end, because the pen log would flag them. They ask for a step-down instead. Employers say nothing about mood. Conditioning is now about logged doses and weight. Army chaplains report fewer 'grey' complaints and more complaints about readiness-programme logs. Casino and sportsbook employers report staff on the gambling indication.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-dose' billings have mostly disappeared, and 'holiday weekend' passes failed as holidays declined. Grey comedy is a nostalgia genre. Sportsbooks cite reduced handle per active account, and two operators disclose incretin exposure as a risk factor. The natty movement has its own folk-revival and long-table supper music scene in Tulsa and Grand Rapids.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists now see the label's 'uncommon' line as permission to look elsewhere for causes. Couples' conflicts have moved from mismatched holidays to whether a coded interruption is worth spending on an anniversary. Some natty–medicated pairings break up over food, not mood.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The pro-access populist bloc claims the Medicare Act. A natty/religious/fat-liberation/privacy coalition targets verified-dose surveillance and the readiness programme, and the House 'Appetite Liberty Caucus' (~30 members, both parties) introduced a federal ban on employer premium conditioning that has not advanced. Candidates are asked whether they are 'natty', and three 2034 House candidates ran on it. The Lilly scandal gave both blocs a common villain without changing either one's position.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access, price-managing and newly punitive toward manufacturers on disclosure. It approved gambling disorder, amycretin and bimagrumab-tirzepatide. It added persistent-gastric-emptying language after the Lilly substudy surfaced and demoted anhedonia to 'uncommon' on pooled data. It is still lenient on off-label brain-health use and the compulsion uses.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate to take the drug. The Medicare Metabolic Health Act made Part D obesity coverage permanent ($195 blended, $35 copay). The optional Medicaid metabolic option at 80% FMAP is adopted by 40 states plus DC. HRSA got $4.2B with a quarterly-visit rider. The ACA cessation mandate continues. The SSA renewal (Nov 2033) runs through 2036.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Conditioning has moved from pharmacy fills to logged injections. A Jan 2034 CMS rule accepts connected-pen dose logs for Medicare continuation and Medicaid waivers, and twelve states now run verified-dose waivers. Indiana and Arkansas still use PDC plus weigh-ins. PBMs sell dose-verification feeds to employers. The circuit split over PDC premium differentials has a cert petition pending. Seven states ban employer premium conditioning, but none restricts its own Medicaid conditions. HHS's privacy office says pen logs are PHI but lawful for 'treatment and payment'.
state.workforce_or_military: The DoD Metabolic Readiness Program has ~165k active-duty participants and now issues connected pens. Body-composition separations are down a further ~10% in FY2034. Religious-accommodation requests reached ~4,200, with most granted with reassignment counselling. Participation is formally voluntary, but separation for failing standards is not. Police and fire contracts in Phoenix, Houston and Chicago were renewed, and Dallas and Atlanta were added.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Section 232 duties on incretin APIs and intermediates continue. Lilly kept its tariff exemption at the cost of the 2033 price concessions while under DOJ scrutiny. Novo pays duty on Danish API. A WTO panel on India's complaint was established in 2033, with a report not before 2035. Chinese amino-acid export controls persist. A Chinese triple agonist is now competing with Indian generics in export markets. US generic entry has slipped to 2035 on FDA complete-response letters.

events.event: Unsealed exhibits in MDL 3094 show Eli Lilly classified a TRIUMPH-4 extension scintigraphy substudy as 'exploratory'. The substudy found delayed gastric emptying up to 12 weeks after stopping 12 mg retatrutide, and Lilly kept it out of its supplemental application summary. Senate HELP calls hearings, DOJ issues a civil investigative demand, and new filings more than double the docket

Oklahoma, Kentucky, Louisiana, South Dakota and Utah pass 'appetite liberty' laws barring employer premiums tied to incretin use, bringing the total to seven states. A 'Fed and Free' Open Table rally of ~20,000 in Tulsa launches a national natty pledge and the open-circle pin

Congress passes the Medicare Metabolic Health Act. It makes Part D obesity coverage permanent from January 2034 at a $195 blended payment and $35 copay, and gives states 80% federal match to cover incretins in Medicaid. The same week, Lilly and Novo sign a renewed Strategic Supply Agreement cutting direct prices to $199 for semaglutide, $249 for tirzepatide, $299 for retatrutide and $129 for oral starts

A CMS rule lets Medicare and Medicaid verify adherence with dose logs from connected autoinjectors instead of pharmacy fills. Lilly launches retatrutide in its 'Link' pen at $299, and it becomes the most common new start for BMI ≥35

FDA approves semaglutide for gambling disorder, the first drug approved for the condition. ASAM names incretins a first-line option for alcohol use disorder. FDA class labelling lists anhedonia as 'uncommon' at maintenance doses on pooled trial data

Novo Nordisk announces a $4.1B no-admission settlement programme for semaglutide gastroparesis and ileus claims in MDL 3094, which now holds ~148,000 claims. Lilly declines to join and a pancreatic-cancer track opens

open_tensions: Coverage now depends on logged injections. Medicare, twelve Medicaid waivers and PBM-fed employer plans use connected-pen data, while Indiana and Arkansas still use fills, seven states ban employer premium conditioning but condition their own Medicaid, and a cert petition on the PDC circuit split could reach verified-dose data next. Locked-out users drift to 503A compounders.

Lilly is both the national champion and a DOJ target. Its tariff exemption and the federal price ceiling rest on a company facing ~100k retatrutide claims and an unresolved disclosure scandal, while generic semaglutide waits on FDA approvals expected in 2035 and the WTO panel on India's complaint is pending.

Public payers are now the default, with Medicare net ≈ $28.2B and Medicaid ≈ $28.9B a year on incretins, and the oldest users carry the bone and muscle risk. Medicare pays for incretin, antiresorptive and soon bimagrumab with no 75+ fracture-outcome trial and no settled price for the 2035 combination launch.

Craving is now a single treatable category spanning food, alcohol and gambling, with shopping and screens off-label. Casinos, distillers and the natty movement each have reasons to contest how far the compulsion label extends, and FDA has not said where it stops.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is sold in the US.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
The ACA preventive mandate still requires plans to cover semaglutide for smoking cessation in two 90-day courses a year.
Participation in the DoD Metabolic Readiness Program is formally voluntary, while separation for failing body-composition standards is not.

prose.headline: The Pen Is Logging: Medicare pays, Lilly apologizes, and America splits into the medicated and the 'natty'
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2034 roughly eighty-seven million American adults, about one in three, take an incretin drug, and for the first time the government pays for more of them than employers do. In November 2033 the temporary Medicare Bridge became permanent Part D coverage, at a blended $195 a month with a $35 copay. The same law offered states eighty cents on the dollar to cover the drugs in Medicaid, and forty states took it. Medicare now spends about twenty-eight billion dollars a year net on these medicines. Most of the new users are poorer and older than the people who used them first.

Prices kept falling, but only in managed steps. The renewed supply deal set direct prices at $199 for semaglutide, $249 for tirzepatide and $299 for retatrutide, the triple agonist that takes off thirty percent of body weight in two years. Lilly accepted those prices while it was under pressure. In March 2033 documents unsealed in the gastroparesis litigation showed that a Lilly study had found stomachs still slow to empty weeks after people stopped the highest retatrutide dose, and the company had labelled the finding exploratory and left it out of the summary it gave regulators. There were hearings, and the Justice Department sent a demand for documents. Lilly kept its tariff exemption and gave up part of its margin. The litigation has grown to about a hundred and forty-eight thousand claims. Novo set aside four billion dollars to settle its share without admitting fault. Lilly is still fighting. Generic semaglutide, expected in 2033, is still waiting on FDA approval of its impurity data.

The biggest change is how adherence is measured. For two years people had gamed the rules by collecting refills they never injected. Now both manufacturers ship pens that record every dose, and since January 2034 Medicare and twelve state Medicaid programmes accept those records as proof of adherence. Benefit managers sell the same data to employers. One appeals court struck down premium penalties based on pharmacy refills, another upheld them, and the pen data is the industry's answer to both rulings. A planned break from the drug now has a billing code.

The flat feeling people called 'the grey' has mostly faded from conversation. Pooled trial data put the real excess at under one percent on standard doses. Clinics now step long-term users down to the lowest dose that works, and the label lists anhedonia as uncommon. Pharmacists ask about it the way they ask about nausea. The same craving circuitry now carries a label for gambling disorder, the first drug approved for it, and addiction doctors name incretins a first-line option for alcohol use disorder. Sportsbooks report less betting per account, and distillers report a sixth year of falling volume.

The people who refuse the drugs have become a culture of their own. 'Natty' started as gym slang for no steroids and now means never on a pen. It comes with an open-circle pin, loose linen, high-waisted 'fed' denim and long Open Table suppers that began in Grand Rapids churches and filled a Tulsa fairground in June 2033. Seven states now bar employers from tying premiums to the drugs. Oklahoma is one of them, and its own Medicaid programme still requires verified doses. About thirty House members call themselves the Appetite Liberty Caucus.

The older users are the hardest to judge. Medicare pays for the incretin, the bone drug and the strength classes, and has approved a muscle-sparing combination due next year. Hip fractures have stopped rising and have not fallen. Seen from outside, the country looks thinner, more sober and more compliant than it did, and most of what it does to stay that way is now on record.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
At 6:10 Denise Harlan presses the pen against her thigh in the kitchen in east Tulsa, counts to ten, and waits for her phone. *SoonerCare: dose verified.* The kettle clicks. Her son is asleep on the couch with his shoes on.

Her first client is Mr. Okafor, seventy-nine. Denise lays out the week on his table: the semaglutide pen, the yellow zoledronic card from his last infusion, the protein shakes his daughter orders by the case. He asks whether he did his shot. She shows him the app. He did, on Sunday. He asks again at eleven.

At lunch she eats half a turkey sandwich in the car and wraps up the other half. A woman at the Braum's drive-through is wearing the open-circle pin on her visor. Denise looks at it longer than she means to.

The afternoon client is younger, forty-four, on the gambling one. He tells her he deleted the betting apps in March and that the Thunder game last night was just a game for once. He says it like he is reporting the weather.

At six she drives to Broken Arrow for her sister Carla's supper. There are long tables in the church fellowship hall and bread torn by hand, and someone has a banjo. Carla is natty and has been since 2029. The pin is on her apron. Carla hands her a plate with everything on it and doesn't say a word about it.

Denise eats the pie, all of it. On the drive home her phone buzzes: *Reminder: 6-month weigh-in due Thursday.* She turns the radio up.
